newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec and most unions agree, others get pay cut.
newsitem.headline: Quebec and most unions agree, others get pay cut.

text.p: The Quebec government and most unions representing its public sector employees agreed on Friday to job cuts that would reduce Quebec's annual payroll costs by C$831 million.
The deal, signed by unions representing 426,000 of 440,000 unionized government workers, stipulated that Quebec would eliminate 15,000 jobs by July 1.

The Quebec legislature also was set to vote special legislation on Friday afternoon, imposing a 6 percent pay cut on politicians, their political staff, judges and doctors. The legislation would also affect 14,000 junior college teachers who by Friday had not signed the job cut agreement.
"It was the time to sign. We had momentum," Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard told reporters after announcing the agreement with most of the unions.

Quebec needed to vote the special legislation in time for Tuesday's budget, in which the government was expected to unveil cost-cutting and revenue-boosting measures to help it meet its objective of a C$2.2 billion deficit for 1997/98.

Simon Prevost, economist with Mouvement Desjardins, told Reuters that aside from C$2.3 billion of cost cuts already announced, Quebec must find C$600 million of additional revenues if it is to meet its deficit objective.
That figure comes after a roughly C$300 million saving expected on debt service costs in 1997/98 -- the result of low Canadian interest rates.
